EXCLUSIVE: NBC is eyeing a fresh spin on a literary classic, with a partially gender-swapped police procedural take on The Great Gatsby in development, Deadline has learned.
The series, titled Gatsby , hails from writer/EPs Jake Coburn and Jason Tracey and Universal Television, a division of Universal Studio Group.
It’s billed as a modern-day police procedural about Det. Jay Gatsby, a devilishly charming investigator with a con-man’s gift for reading human behavior, and decorated New York State Police Det. Nicole “Nicky” Carraway, who was born to be a cop but dreams of becoming a writer. The gender-swapped character here is Nicky, a female counterpart to bond salesman Nick Carraway, who as neighbor to enigmatic self-made millionaire Jay Gatsby, serves as narrator to F. Scott Fitzgerald’s tragic 1925 novel The Great Gatsby . The book finds Nick moving to the fictional Long Island neighborhood of West Egg, where he becomes drawn into the world of Gatsby amid his efforts to rekindle a romance with his cousin, Daisy Buchanan. Watch on Deadline
Considered one of the ‘Great American Novels,’ Gatsby has been adapted for the screen on myriad occasions, dating back to a 1926 silent film from Herbert Brenon, though mostly for film. The most famous adaptations are a Francis Ford Coppola-penned Paramount version starring Robert Redford, Bruce Dern and Mia Farrow, which released in 1974, and Baz Luhrmann’s big-budget 2013 take for Warner Bros. starring Leonardo DiCaprio, Tobey Maguire and Carey Mulligan.
An NBC veteran who has worked on a number of their series, Coburn comes to Gatsby after serving as co-showrunner and executive producer of their procedural The Hunting Party , which ran for two seasons. Before that, he was co-creator and executive producer of their crime drama The Endgame , as well as executive producer on Barbarians (Netflix), Biohackers (Netflix) and Quantico (ABC). He began his TV writing career on ABC’s Dirty Sexy Money before segueing to Gossip Girl , where he rose to the level of supervising producer. He has also written for the Arrow and Dynasty and, in addition to writing TV, has published two award-winning teen novels. He is repped by UTA and Brecheen Feldman Breimer.
Tracey most recently served as an executive producer on the ABC series RJ Decker . Prior to that, he was the creator and showrunner of CBS’ CSI: Vegas , produced by Jerry Bruckheimer, where he was under an overall deal. His pilot Alive , starring Ryan Phillippe, was also produced for CBS. An executive producer on Elementary for all seven seasons, he worked earlier in his career on Burn Notice , Justice and Cold Case . He is repped by CAA, Lit Entertainment Group and Jacobson Teller Hoberman.
